problem_text:
A logistics firm must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical component over an operational window of 18 consecutive days.  
The starting stock at the dawn of the planning interval is 41 units.  
On any given day \( t = 1, \dots, 18 \), the supplier permits the firm to issue a procurement request, with the quantity required to fall between 9 and 62 units.  
Nevertheless, every order placed is subject to a lead time of 1 day before it becomes available for fulfilling requirements or augmenting stock.  
The daily requirement for the component is specified as:  
* Day 1: 31 units  
* Day 2: 41 units  
* Day 3: 19 units  
* Day 4: 43 units  
* Day 5: 56 units  
* Day 6: 57 units  
* Day 7: 11 units  
* Day 8: 57 units  
* Day 9: 40 units  
* Day 10: 18 units  
* Day 11: 10 units  
* Day 12: 15 units  
* Day 13: 45 units  
* Day 14: 11 units  
* Day 15: 18 units  
* Day 16: 58 units  
* Day 17: 17 units  
* Day 18: 13 units  

Stockouts are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement is considered lost and will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the entire planning window, component quantities may be treated as continuous values, and the total physical stock held at any moment must remain within the storage facility’s limit of 43 units.

Specifically, on the sixth day, the maximum allowable order quantity is 59 units.  
On the twelfth day, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 24 units.

The aggregate expenditure over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement cost, charged at 1 per unit ordered; the storage cost, charged at 3 per unit transferred from one day to the next; and the penalty for unmet demand, charged at 6 per unit of lost requirement.  
The objective is to ascertain the optimal procurement quantity for each day and to monitor the consequent stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expenditure.
